title: Reporting verbs and their patterns
tagline: Swap 'said' for a verb that shows what someone actually did with their words.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations
Reading & Use of English Part 1 — multiple-choice cloze
Speaking Part 3 — reporting what a partner suggested or agreed
why: Repeating 'said' and 'told' through a whole story or essay sounds flat, and it hides what a person actually did with their words: did they warn, admit, refuse or insist? B2 First rewards the precise verb, and Part 4 regularly turns a line of direct speech into one of these patterns. Losing marks here is usually about the pattern, not the meaning — the wrong preposition, or an infinitive where a gerund belongs.

rows.label: Example
cells: advised us not to be late

rows.label: Typical error
cells: advised to be late — missing sb (wrong)

diagrams.title: Blaming someone: accuse / suspect
diagrams.caption: They accused the goalkeeper of missing the penalty.

head: Pattern
Verbs
Example
rows: insist on, apologise for, admit to
He insisted on paying for the tickets.
warn, advise, persuade, remind, encourage, tell
Miss Vega warned us not to be late.
Liam offered to design the poster.

examples.text: Nadia suggested moving the training session to the morning.
The coach advised us to warm up properly before the match.
Miss Vega recommended reading the whole article before the debate.
Liam finally admitted losing the school key.
Sofia denied sending the message, but her name was on it.
Two students accused the referee of favouring the other team.
Mateo promised to send the notes before the exam.
Nadia offered to translate the poem for the magazine.
He refused to apologise, even after Miss Vega spoke to him.
The lifeguard warned the swimmers not to go past the flags.
Can you remind me to bring my ID card tomorrow?
Her older brother persuaded her to apply for the scholarship.

watch_out.wrong: She suggested me to join the debate team.
watch_out.right: She suggested joining the debate team. / She suggested that I join the debate team.
watch_out.why: Suggest never takes sb + to-infinitive; use -ing or a that-clause.

watch_out.wrong: He denied to take the money.
watch_out.why: Deny is followed by -ing, not a to-infinitive.

watch_out.wrong: They accused him to cheat in the test.
watch_out.right: They accused him of cheating in the test.
watch_out.why: Accuse needs sb + of + -ing, not a bare to-infinitive.

watch_out.wrong: She recommended to book the tickets early.
watch_out.why: Recommend (without an object) is followed by -ing or a that-clause, never to-infinitive.

watch_out.wrong: He warned to be careful on the ice.
watch_out.right: He warned us to be careful on the ice.
watch_out.why: Warn almost always needs an object (sb) before the to-infinitive.

watch_out.wrong: I apologised to be late for rehearsal.
watch_out.right: I apologised for being late for rehearsal.
watch_out.why: Apologise is followed by for + -ing, not a to-infinitive.

dialogue.title: Who said what about the group project
dialogue.context: Miss Vega is asking Mateo, Sofia and Liam to explain a mix-up over their class presentation on the Nazca Lines.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: So, Mateo, you suggested changing the topic on Monday. Why didn't the others know?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I did tell them! Sofia even agreed to email you about it.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: I never agreed to do that — I only said I'd think about it.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Actually, Nadia warned us not to leave it until the last minute, remember?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: She did. And I admitted forgetting about the deadline in front of everyone.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Liam, didn't you offer to finish the slides yourself?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: I did, but then Mateo insisted on redoing the whole design.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Because the first version was a mess. I'm not going to deny saying that.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Nobody's accusing anyone of ruining the project, Mateo — we just need a plan now.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good. I recommend finishing this by Friday, and no more surprises.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Deal. I promise to send the final file tonight.

items.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ arrive early for the exam.
Liam denied ___ the message before the meeting.
They accused the goalkeeper ___ the match.
The coach insisted ___ extra training before the tournament.
The manager warned the players ___ late again.

practice.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.

items.sentence: The manager warned the staff ___ (not/be) late for the meeting.
Sofia admitted ___ (forget) her lines during the play.
Liam's parents encouraged him ___ (try) out for the football team.
The police accused the driver ___ (speed) through the town centre.
Nadia offered ___ (help) with the school fundraiser.
The coach insisted ___ (train) every morning before school.
Mateo apologised ___ (miss) the rehearsal on Tuesday.
Mateo denied ___ (not/do) his homework, insisting he had finished it early.

practice.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first. Use the word given. Do not change it. Use between two and five words.

items.first: 'I'll help you carry the boxes,' said Liam.
'You should apply for the exchange programme,' the teacher told Nadia.
'I didn't take Sofia's charger,' said Mateo.
'You must hand in the essay by Friday,' said Miss Vega.
'You broke the window, Liam!' said Nadia.

summary: Reporting verbs replace 'said' with a verb that shows what someone actually did: suggested, denied, warned, offered.
Each verb has its own pattern — -ing, to-infinitive, sb + to-infinitive, or sb + of + -ing — and mixing them up is the most common mistake.
Suggest, recommend, admit and deny take -ing (or a that-clause), never sb + to-infinitive.
Accuse and suspect need sb + of + -ing; warn, advise, persuade and remind need sb + to-infinitive.
In Part 4, the reporting verb given as the key word usually tells you which pattern the answer needs.
